title: Isaiah Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 20.

questions.question: Who sent Tartan to Ashdod according to Isaiah 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Sargon the king of Assyria
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:1 states that Sargon the king of Assyria sent Tartan to Ashdod.

questions.question: What city did Tartan fight against and take?
questions.correctAnswer: Ashdod
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:1 says Tartan came unto Ashdod, fought against it, and took it.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Isaiah to remove from his loins?
questions.correctAnswer: Sackcloth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 records the LORD commanding Isaiah to loose the sackcloth from off his loins.

questions.question: What did Isaiah remove from his foot as commanded by the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Shoe
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 states that Isaiah put off his shoe from his foot as the LORD commanded.

questions.question: How did Isaiah walk after removing sackcloth and shoe?
questions.correctAnswer: Naked and barefoot
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 says Isaiah walked naked and barefoot after obeying the LORD's command.

questions.question: For how many years did Isaiah walk naked and barefoot as a sign?
questions.correctAnswer: Three years
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:3 states Isaiah walked naked and barefoot for three years for a sign and wonder.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah was commanded to put on sackcloth and shoes.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 shows the LORD commanded Isaiah to remove sackcloth and shoes, not to put them on.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah's walking naked and barefoot was a sign upon Egypt and Ethiopia.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:3 says Isaiah's walking naked and barefoot was a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia.

questions.question: Who is identified as the son of Amoz in Isaiah 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 identifies Isaiah as the son of Amoz.

questions.question: What is the primary reason Isaiah walked naked and barefoot according to the LORD?
options: As a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia
To punish the people of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: As a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:3 states that Isaiah's walking naked and barefoot was a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia.

questions.question: True or False: Tartan was sent to Jerusalem to fight by Sargon the king of Assyria.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:1 explains Tartan was sent to Ashdod, not Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does the LORD instruct Isaiah to do first in Isaiah 20?
options: Loose the sackcloth from his loins
questions.correctAnswer: Loose the sackcloth from his loins
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 shows the LORD's instruction begins with loosening the sackcloth from Isaiah's loins before putting off the shoe.

questions.question: In Isaiah 20, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Loose the sackcloth from thy loins
Put off thy shoe from thy foot
questions.correctAnswer: Loose the sackcloth from thy loins
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 records the order: first loose the sackcloth, then put off the shoe, then walk naked and barefoot.

questions.question: Who is described as the king that sent Tartan in Isaiah 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Sargon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:1 identifies Sargon the king of Assyria as the one who sent Tartan.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah walked barefoot but clothed in sackcloth for three years.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2-3 says Isaiah walked naked and barefoot after loosening sackcloth and removing shoes.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What event does Isaiah 20:1 describe that sets the context for the message given to Isaiah?
options: The fall of Ashdod to the king of Assyria
The capture of Jerusalem by Babylon
The exile of the Israelites to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The fall of Ashdod to the king of Assyria
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:1 explains that in the year Tartan came to Ashdod, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, and took Ashdod, setting the historical context for Isaiah's prophecy.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 20:2, what symbolic action did the LORD instruct Isaiah to perform?
questions.correctAnswer: To walk naked and barefoot
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 states that God commanded Isaiah to loose the sackcloth and remove his shoes, then walk naked and barefoot as a sign.

questions.question: What reason does Isaiah 20:3 give for Isaiah walking naked and barefoot for three years?
options: As a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia
To mourn for the people of Israel
To show repentance for Israel’s sins
questions.correctAnswer: As a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:3 explains that Isaiah's nakedness and barefoot walking were a prophetic sign and wonder directed at Egypt and Ethiopia.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 20:4 describe the fate of the Egyptians and Ethiopians at the hands of the king of Assyria?
options: They will be led away naked, barefoot, and with their buttocks uncovered
They will form an alliance with Assyria
They will defeat the king of Assyria
They will be spared from captivity
questions.correctAnswer: They will be led away naked, barefoot, and with their buttocks uncovered
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:4 indicates that the king of Assyria will capture Egyptians and Ethiopians young and old, leading them away naked and barefoot, exposing them to shame.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 20:3 and 20:4, what does Isaiah’s symbolic action teach about trust in God versus reliance on worldly powers?
options: Trusting in God is essential because reliance on Egypt or Ethiopia will lead to shame and captivity.
Isaiah’s action shows that worldly powers are more dependable than God.
It means that physical strength guarantees victory over enemies.
God encourages alliances with powerful nations for security.
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting in God is essential because reliance on Egypt or Ethiopia will lead to shame and captivity.
questions.explanation: Verses 20:3-4 use Isaiah’s symbolic nakedness to show that trusting in Egypt and Ethiopia (worldly powers) will result in disgrace and captivity, emphasizing reliance on God instead.

questions.question: What lesson about humility can believers learn from Isaiah’s obedience to walk naked and barefoot for three years as described in Isaiah 20:2-3?
options: Humility involves obediently following God’s commands even when it involves personal shame.
Humility means hiding from difficult situations.
Believers should avoid public actions that cause shame.
Humility is only about quiet prayer and meditation.
questions.correctAnswer: Humility involves obediently following God’s commands even when it involves personal shame.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2-3 shows Isaiah humbling himself by obeying God’s command to walk naked and barefoot, teaching believers that true humility may require costly obedience.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 20:5, what will be the emotional response of Egypt to the captivity by Assyria?
options: Fear and shame toward Ethiopia and Egypt’s own glory
questions.correctAnswer: Fear and shame toward Ethiopia and Egypt’s own glory
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:5 states that Egypt will be afraid and ashamed of Ethiopia, their hope, and of Egypt’s own glory due to the captivity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 20:6 reveal about the perception of those living on 'this isle' regarding the king of Assyria?
options: They fear how to escape the king of Assyria despite fleeing for help.
They feel completely secure from Assyria’s attacks.
They plan to join forces with Assyria.
They are unaware of Assyria’s power.
questions.correctAnswer: They fear how to escape the king of Assyria despite fleeing for help.
questions.explanation: Verse 20:6 indicates that inhabitants will question how they can escape Assyria despite fleeing for help, highlighting their fear and desperation.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah’s prophecy in Isaiah 20 teaches that pride in human alliances leads to downfall and shame.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:3-5 shows that reliance on Egypt and Ethiopia (human alliances) will lead to shame and captivity, teaching that pride in such alliances leads to downfall.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah was commanded to wear sackcloth and shoes as a sign to Egypt and Ethiopia.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 states the LORD told Isaiah to loose the sackcloth and remove his shoes, walking naked and barefoot, not to wear them.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah’s prophetic sign was intended to last only a few days.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:3 specifies that Isaiah walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and wonder, not just a few days.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 20:4 suggest about the consequences of trusting in foreign nations for security?
options: It leads to humiliation and captivity.
It results in wealth and prosperity.
questions.correctAnswer: It leads to humiliation and captivity.
questions.explanation: Verse 20:4 describes how Assyria will lead away Egyptian and Ethiopian captives naked and barefoot, symbolizing the shame and defeat that come from misplaced trust.

questions.question: How can Isaiah 20:2-4 encourage believers facing shame or hardship for their faith?
options: To trust God even when it requires obedience that involves personal sacrifice or shame.
To avoid any situation that causes discomfort.
To seek approval from others above all.
To rely on political powers for safety.
questions.correctAnswer: To trust God even when it requires obedience that involves personal sacrifice or shame.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2-4 shows Isaiah’s obedience despite shame teaches believers to trust God and obey Him even in difficult circumstances.

questions.question: What practical lesson about integrity does Isaiah 20:2-3 provide for believers today?
options: Integrity involves faithfully following God’s commands regardless of embarrassment or social pressure.
Integrity means only doing what is easy and socially acceptable.
Integrity is about avoiding uncomfortable truths.
Integrity means seeking human praise above all.
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity involves faithfully following God’s commands regardless of embarrassment or social pressure.
questions.explanation: Isaiah’s obedience to walk naked and barefoot demonstrates integrity by obeying God regardless of personal discomfort or shame (Isaiah 20:2-3).

questions.question: What does Isaiah 20:5 teach about misplaced hope in human strength or alliances?
options: Misplaced hope leads to fear and shame when those alliances fail.
Human strength is always reliable for security.
Hope in alliances brings unshakable peace.
Fear and shame come only from spiritual failure.
questions.correctAnswer: Misplaced hope leads to fear and shame when those alliances fail.
questions.explanation: Verse 20:5 explains that Egypt will be afraid and ashamed of Ethiopia, their hope, showing that misplaced trust leads to disappointment and disgrace.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 20.

questions.question: What did Isaiah do as a sign for three years according to the LORD's command?
options: Built an altar in the temple
Proclaimed a fast to the people
questions.correctAnswer: Walked naked and barefoot
questions.explanation: Isaiah walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia, as commanded by the LORD (Isaiah 20:3).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 20, who led away the Egyptians and Ethiopians as captives?
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Assyria
questions.explanation: The king of Assyria is prophesied to lead away Egyptians and Ethiopians, both young and old, as captives (Isaiah 20:4).

questions.question: What was the condition of the captives taken from Egypt and Ethiopia by Assyria?
options: Naked and barefoot, with their buttocks uncovered
questions.correctAnswer: Naked and barefoot, with their buttocks uncovered
questions.explanation: The captives were taken naked and barefoot, with their buttocks uncovered, symbolizing their shame (Isaiah 20:4).

questions.question: What emotion will Egypt feel towards Ethiopia and itself according to Isaiah 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Fear and shame
questions.explanation: Egypt will be afraid and ashamed of Ethiopia, which it expected to help, and of Egypt, its own glory (Isaiah 20:5).

questions.question: Who does the 'inhabitant of this isle' refer to in Isaiah 20:6, and what will he say?
options: A Philistine or coastal dweller, saying their expected help is futile
An Egyptian official, proclaiming victory over Assyria
An Assyrian soldier, boasting of conquest
questions.correctAnswer: A Philistine or coastal dweller, saying their expected help is futile
questions.explanation: The 'inhabitant of this isle' likely refers to a resident of the Philistine coast who realizes their hope in Egypt and Ethiopia to escape Assyria is futile (Isaiah 20:6).

questions.question: In Isaiah 20:2, what specific actions did the LORD command Isaiah to perform as symbolic acts?
options: Loose the sackcloth and put off his shoe
Build an altar and sacrifice a lamb
Shout a prophecy at the city gates
questions.correctAnswer: Loose the sackcloth and put off his shoe
questions.explanation: The LORD commanded Isaiah to loosen his sackcloth and remove his shoe, then walk naked and barefoot as a prophetic sign (Isaiah 20:2).

questions.question: Which Assyrian king is mentioned in Isaiah 20 as sending Tartan to fight Ashdod?
questions.correctAnswer: Sargon
questions.explanation: Sargon, king of Assyria, sent Tartan to Ashdod to fight and capture it (Isaiah 20:1).

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah's walking naked and barefoot was meant to shame the people of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah's naked and barefoot walk was a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia, not Israel (Isaiah 20:3).

questions.question: True or False: The prophecy in Isaiah 20 implies that Egypt and Ethiopia will fail to provide the expected help against Assyria.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The inhabitants will be afraid and ashamed of Egypt and Ethiopia, their expectation and glory, indicating they will fail to help against Assyria (Isaiah 20:5-6).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book contains a prophecy of a servant of the LORD walking naked as a sign, similar to Isaiah 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 13:1-7 describes Jeremiah wearing a linen girdle and hiding it, symbolizing judgment, paralleling Isaiah's symbolic nakedness as a prophetic sign (Isaiah 20:2-3).

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'naked' in Isaiah 20 carries connotations of:
questions.correctAnswer: Shame and humiliation
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'naked' (עוֹרֵר) in Isaiah 20 implies exposure and shame, highlighting the humiliation of Egypt and Ethiopia's defeat (Isaiah 20:4).

questions.question: What literary device is predominantly used in Isaiah 20 to communicate the prophecy through Isaiah’s actions?
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic symbolic enactment
questions.explanation: Isaiah acts out the prophecy by walking naked and barefoot, a prophetic symbolic enactment conveying the message visually (Isaiah 20:2-3).

questions.question: How does Isaiah 20 foreshadow the later fall of Egypt and Ethiopia as nations in biblical history?
options: By predicting their captivity and humiliation by Assyria
By promising their eternal victory over enemies
By foretelling their alliance against Israel
questions.correctAnswer: By predicting their captivity and humiliation by Assyria
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20 prophesies that Assyria will lead Egypt and Ethiopia away captive, foreshadowing their historical subjugation (Isaiah 20:4-5).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of trusting in human powers rather than God, similar to the warning in Isaiah 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 17:12-13
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:12-13 describes kings who give their power to the beast, reflecting the folly of relying on political or military powers rather than God, similar to Isaiah 20's warning against trusting Egypt and Ethiopia.

questions.question: In the historical context of Isaiah 20, what was the significance of Assyria capturing Ashdod?
options: It demonstrated Assyria's expanding influence in the Philistine region
It marked the end of Egyptian domination over Judah
It was the first battle of the Babylonian exile
It led to the destruction of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrated Assyria's expanding influence in the Philistine region
questions.explanation: The capture of Ashdod by Assyria under Sargon's command showed Assyria's growing control over the coastal Philistine cities, affecting regional power dynamics (Isaiah 20:1).

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific action did Isaiah take as a prophetic sign according to Isaiah 20:2?
options: He built an altar to the LORD
He shouted a warning to the people
questions.correctAnswer: He walked naked and barefoot
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 explicitly states that Isaiah was commanded by the LORD to loose the sackcloth from his loins and put off his shoe, and he walked naked and barefoot as a sign.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 20:1, who sent Tartan to fight against Ashdod?
questions.correctAnswer: Sargon, king of Assyria
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:1 states that Tartan was sent by Sargon, king of Assyria, to come to Ashdod and fight against it.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 20:3 reveal about the duration Isaiah walked naked and barefoot?
questions.correctAnswer: Three years
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:3 clearly mentions that Isaiah walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 20:4 say the king of Assyria will do to the Egyptians and Ethiopians?
options: Lead them away as prisoners, naked and barefoot
questions.correctAnswer: Lead them away as prisoners, naked and barefoot
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:4 states that the king of Assyria will lead away Egyptians and Ethiopians prisoners, young and old, naked and barefoot, to the shame of Egypt.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Isaiah’s act of walking naked and barefoot for three years as described in Isaiah 20:2-3?
options: The doctrine of prophetic sign acts as a divine revelation
The doctrine of atonement through sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of prophetic sign acts as a divine revelation
questions.explanation: Isaiah’s act serves as a prophetic sign and wonder, a physical demonstration ordained by God to reveal future events, illustrating the doctrine that God uses signs to communicate His will (Isaiah 20:2-3).

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God commanding Isaiah to act as a sign in Isaiah 20:2?
options: God’s sovereignty in using human agents
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty in using human agents
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 reveals God's sovereign control over history and His use of human agents like Isaiah to fulfill His prophetic purposes.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 20:5, what will the Egyptians feel toward Ethiopia and Egypt’s former hopes?
questions.correctAnswer: Afraid and ashamed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:5 states that Egyptians will be afraid and ashamed of Ethiopia, their expectation, and Egypt, their glory, indicating the futility of relying on these nations.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 20:6 portray the reaction of the inhabitants of the isle in the day of Assyrian invasion?
options: They will recognize their misplaced trust and fear escape
They will celebrate their alliance with Assyria
They will be indifferent to the events
They will rise up against Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: They will recognize their misplaced trust and fear escape
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:6 describes the inhabitants of the isle acknowledging their false hope in fleeing to Assyria for help and questioning how they shall escape.

questions.question: What combined theological insight is gained by synthesizing Isaiah 20:3 and Isaiah 20:4 about God’s judgment?
options: God uses prophetic signs to reveal impending judgment and humiliation of nations
God promises restoration to Egypt and Ethiopia
God emphasizes ritual purity for deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: God uses prophetic signs to reveal impending judgment and humiliation of nations
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:3 shows Isaiah’s prophetic sign of nakedness, and 20:4 explains that Assyria will humiliate Egypt and Ethiopia, revealing God's use of signs to warn of coming judgment.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human pride and political alliances is highlighted by the combined message of Isaiah 20:5 and Isaiah 20:6?
options: Reliance on human powers for salvation leads to fear and shame
Human pride is rewarded by God
God is indifferent to nations’ political schemes
questions.correctAnswer: Reliance on human powers for salvation leads to fear and shame
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:5 and 20:6 together teach that trusting in human powers like Ethiopia, Egypt, or Assyria results in fear, shame, and despair instead of deliverance.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 20:1 contribute to the historical narrative that supports God's providence in Isaiah’s prophecy?
options: It situates the prophecy in a real Assyrian military campaign
It describes a miraculous event unrelated to history
It emphasizes the peaceful reign of Sargon
It focuses on Israel’s internal affairs
questions.correctAnswer: It situates the prophecy in a real Assyrian military campaign
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:1 grounds the prophecy within a historical context of Assyria's military action, affirming God’s providence over nations.

questions.question: What apologetic response does Isaiah 20:4-6 provide against the sceptic who claims that God’s people can rely on Egypt and Ethiopia for deliverance?
options: God’s word predicts that these nations will be humiliated and unable to save
God promises Egypt and Ethiopia as eternal allies
God’s people should trust only in military strength
God’s people are left to their own devices
questions.correctAnswer: God’s word predicts that these nations will be humiliated and unable to save
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:4-6 teaches that Egypt and Ethiopia will be led away as captives and bring shame, disproving reliance on them for help, countering sceptical claims.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by His declaration in Isaiah 20:5 that Egypt’s glory will become a source of shame?
options: God’s justice in humbling the proud
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in humbling the proud
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:5 shows God’s justice in exposing and humbling the pride of Egypt, turning their glory into shame.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 20:2-3 foreshadow the redemptive theme of humiliation and nakedness seen ultimately in Christ’s suffering?
options: Isaiah’s nakedness symbolizes the humiliation Christ would endure for humanity’s salvation
Isaiah’s walk signifies a joyful celebration
Isaiah’s sign indicates a political alliance
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah’s nakedness symbolizes the humiliation Christ would endure for humanity’s salvation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2-3’s emphasis on nakedness and shame prophetically foreshadows Christ’s humiliation and naked suffering on the cross as part of redemption (cf. John 19:23-24).

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Isaiah 20:6 illustrate regarding the futility of trusting in worldly powers for salvation throughout Scripture?
options: It continues the biblical theme of trusting God alone for deliverance
It introduces a new concept of political salvation
It contradicts earlier promises of peace
questions.correctAnswer: It continues the biblical theme of trusting God alone for deliverance
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:6 reflects the broader biblical narrative that reliance on human powers such as Assyria for salvation is futile, emphasizing faith in God alone (cf. Psalm 118:8).
